From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Draft order form + DPA questions

Rachel / Marcus — I reviewed Aurora's DPA and the attached SCCs. High-level summary of redlines and open items below; full annotated doc attached.

Summary (high level):
- Role allocation: Redwood can accept "processor" status for the hosted inference service, but we need clarity in the Order Form on which services (hosted, dedicated, private) are in scope. Suggest explicit service list in Exhibit A.
- Sub-processor notification: Agree to provide a rolling list 30 days prior for major sub-processors; we will not provide 30-day notice for ephemeral infra providers (catch-all language required).
- Audit rights: Accept audit requests limited to one coordinated audit per 12 months and limited scope (security controls, not business KPIs). Aurora's quarterly window is too broad; propose a compromise of annual + ad hoc with defined evidence set.
- Data retention & telemetry: Telemetry used for product improvements should be pseudonymized; any persistent identifiers require Aurora's sign-off.
- SCCs: Minor drafting tweaks to ensure our subprocessors are covered; see proposed clause in the attached.

Open asks for Aurora: 
1) Can you confirm which Redwood deployment modes your purchase will cover (hosted API vs. dedicated vs. private)?
2) Provide the data flow diagram referenced in the DPA (helps with TIA scope).
3) Confirm whether Aurora requires log-level export for audit requests or whether summarized evidence is acceptable.

I've attached redwood_dpa_comments_aurora_v1.docx with inline comments and a proposed "one-audit-per-year" clause. I'm marking the SCCs edits as "subject to product sign-off."

Attachments: redwood_dpa_comments_aurora_v1.docx

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Draft order form + DPA questions

Laura — thanks for the thorough review. Quick answers inline and attachments below.

1) Deployment mode: We plan to sign for hosted API only for the initial term (Order Form line item 1). If we expand to Dedicated later, we will request an amendment.
2) Data flow: See attached aurora_data_flow_v1.pdf — it shows PII sources, enrichment steps, and downstream analytics recipients.
3) Audit evidence: We prefer log-level export for specific incidents; for routine audits we can accept summarized evidence. We understand your proposal for annual audits + scoped ad hoc for incidents.

On SCCs/roles: We can accept the proposed one-audit-per-year compromise but need the sub-processor notification window to be operationally realistic. If Redwood can publish an internal sub-processor roster and a change log we can accept a 14-day notification for major changes.

Attached: aurora_data_flow_v1.pdf

Next steps: if you share your annotated DPA with tracked changes we will respond to each redline. Also, can Redwood provide the short SCCs amendment language so our legal can review quickly?

Regards,
Samir

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft order form + DPA questions

Samir / Rachel — adding product/security input. We reviewed Aurora's data flow and have three operational proposals that we believe limit risk while meeting Aurora's needs: 

1) Scoped sub-processor roster + change log: Redwood will publish a customer-facing sub-processor roster and maintain a 14-day change log for major sub-processors (those with access to customer data). Ephemeral infra (cloud compute instances) are excluded.

2) Audit scope language (proposed): "Customer may request one coordinated audit per 12-month period covering technical and organizational controls relevant to the Services in scope. Redwood will provide evidence artifacts (configurations, control tests, summarized logs). Log-level exports will be produced only for incident-driven audits subject to legal process and minimization requirements." (See proposed_sccs_clause.txt attached)

3) Data processing scope: We'll add a short schedule listing 'Hosted API' only for this Order Form and reference a future amendment for other modes. That reduces TIA scope substantially.

If Aurora is OK with those three items we can prepare tracked-change DPA and a short SCCs amendment for signature.

Attachments: proposed_sccs_clause.txt

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Product Manager, Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
